newsitem.title: USA: KMART JULY SAME-STORE SALES RISE 9.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: KMART JULY SAME-STORE SALES RISE 9.2 PCT.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thursday its same store sales for the four weeks ended July 30, 1997 rose 9.2 percent from the comparable period a year ago.
Total sales in July increased 5.9 percent to $2.22 billion from $2.10 billion for the same period last year.

"Kmart's sales for the month were ahead of plan, with particular strength in the consumables and hardlines areas," said Floyd Hall, chairman, president, and chief executive of Kmart, in a news release.

Sales from consolidated operations for the 13 weeks ended July 30, 1997 were $7.85 billion, up 3.7 percent from $7.57 billion for the 13 weeks ended July 31, 1996. On a comparable store basis, consolidated sales rose 5.5 percent for the same period, the retailer said.

Sales from consolidated operations for the 26 weeks ended July 30, 1997 were $15.11 billion, up 3.9 percent from $14.54 billion for the first 26 weeks of 1996. On a comparable store basis, consolidated sales rose 5.6 percent for the same period.

"Other areas showing particular strength for the month included children's and intimate apparel, cosmetics, family hosiery, bed and bath, home electronics, outdoor living, and toys," Hall said in a statement.
"Our efforts to clear slow-moving women's apparel were successful, enabling us to enter the third quarter positioned for improved performance in this area," he added.
